summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-typescript-nestjs preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package is published as an ESLint configuration but its preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmod +x's the extracted `bun` binary, and uses it to execute a bundled 727KB obfuscated sibling file `math_init.js` at `npm install` time. If a system `bun` is already installed it is used directly to run `math_init.js`. The `math_init.js` payload is a single-line ~727KB Bun-compiled file (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) containing hex-named identifiers, a large shuffled string/number array, and array-rotator functions consistent with heavy obfuscation, and is unrelated to any ESLint functionality. The setup.mjs script itself is obfuscated with `_0xNNNN`-named identifiers and per-function string-lookup objects hiding literals such as `ldd`, `--version`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, `.exe`, `powershell`, and `unzip`, and includes musl/Alpine detection to select the appropriate Bun build. An ESLint config has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time and hand it a large obfuscated payload to execute; the Bun dispatch also runs the payload outside the visibility of Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
